before_live_sample.interpretation: Wall-time stack residency on the coordinator, not whole-process CPU percentages; workers mostly blocked.

intermediate_query_sample.interpretation: After argv projection, during a requestProcInfo workload; not directly comparable to the earlier live idle/page sample.

request_proc_info.method: Three sequential ChromeUtils.requestProcInfo() calls in an isolated chrome automation sandbox; same offline page, fresh profile per variant. No profiling during these timing runs.
limitations: One ordered run per variant, no shuffled repetitions or confidence intervals.
Timing capture precedes the final proc-FD-alias dependency guard; that guard is separately regression-tested and the final binary is functionally tested on Wikipedia.
The old batch has no per-iteration progress, so no individual old call duration or exact speedup is claimed.

native_input.method: Ten native clicks on the same offline count button; source system-uptime timestamps from mouse release to emitted native title change. CUA holds the mouse down for roughly 50 ms, excluded.

after.note: Intermediate titles can coalesce; this is not a presentation timestamp.

limitations: Intermediate title updates can coalesce; only emitted titles have exact matched timings.
Not screen-present latency, FPS or a native-host comparison.
Small sample; after run has a 234 ms first response and is not uniformly fast.

ipc_regression.scenario: socketpair sends one byte; recvmsg supplies a 2 MiB iovec capacity
ipc_regression.overflow: UINT64_MAX length returns EINVAL and does not consume the queued byte
ipc_regression.scope: Confirmed Linux compatibility bug; no proof that it explains every Firefox child-process launch warning.

validation.normal_wikipedia_navigation: Wikipedia portal -> English main page visible with original profile and no Marionette
validation.reused: Unchanged CPU/HVF and Vulkan tests from the previous acceptance; not rerun.

remaining: Firefox content/utility subprocess launch retries still appear.

privacy: Only aggregate data and artifact hashes are published. Browser profiles, raw traces, argv, host addresses and browsing logs remain local.
